note: A tune that steps down from Sol to Do, learned in named stages at 40 bpm, then a line of the singer's own from the low Do, Mi and Sol over I IV V I at 40 bpm. The chords are tokens counted the long way, the old Key choice is moves (key any, tempo 40 to 60), the line about another key opens with {{?key}}, and the made-up line carries the one care line.

exercise.title: A Sol tune, then your own line
exercise.why: A tune that steps down from Sol to Do puts both notes in your ear first, so your own line from Do, Mi and Sol has a start and an end to choose from.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then press Play again and sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Practice until you can start on {{5}} without hearing it first.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, and the tune still steps down from {{5}} to {{1}}.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}, and {{chord:V}} the 5th, built on {{5}}.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. Make up your own line from the low {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}}, one that moves when the chords do and ends on {{1}} when {{chord:I}} comes back. Sing it on "oo".
_Don't reach for high notes: the three low ones are enough for a line._
